# Workflow Overview

GitHub Actions separates pull-request validation, validation of `develop`, nightly publication, release packaging, and storage cleanup. The [workflow files](workflows/) are the source of truth for triggers, job dependencies, permissions, and implementation details.

## Workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose and main elements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Feature - Sanity check](workflows/branch.yml) | Pull requests targeting `develop` | Validates the pull-request head with a Linux Docker build and automated tests, and containerized directory backend tests against the Firestore emulator. `Feature Ready` depends only on the Linux job. |
| [macOS - Native builds](workflows/macos-build.yml) | Reusable workflow call | Builds, tests, and packages separate experimental Apple Silicon and Intel x86_64 applications at the requested source SHA. Used by develop validation and nightly publication. |
| [Linux ARM64 - Pi 5 candidate](workflows/arm64.yml) | Reusable call from Develop - Sanity, or manual dispatch | Native ARM64 Docker compilation, hardware-AES known-answer and existing CTests using the default `gl1` renderer. A companion x86 Docker build supplies the client and resolver for cross-architecture verification. Uploads a separate architecture-labelled ARM candidate. Software-rendered CI does not certify Pi 5 V3D, peripherals, performance or independent crypto review. |
| [Develop - Build Container Image](workflows/develop-build-image.yml) | Tool-input changes on `develop`, or manual dispatch from `develop` | Independently publishes Linux amd64, Linux ARM64, Windows cross, and native Windows transport tool images. Existing immutable versions are reused. Each package has a `latest` convenience alias. |
| [Develop - Sanity](workflows/develop.yml) | Push to `develop` | Uses prebuilt tool images and runs independent Unit/basic, Common/local-game, and Network/server-client Linux jobs. Unit/basic includes the full-runtime main-menu smoke. A Debug compilation supplies the lint-equivalent check. Platform jobs retain native Windows transport CTests, the experimental macOS build/tests/package, and the ARM64 candidate workflow. All checks and matching tool-image availability must pass to advance `sanity` and enable the nightly scheduler. |
| [Develop - Nightly Scheduler](workflows/develop-nightly-scheduler.yml) | Every four hours while enabled, or manual dispatch | Requests a nightly build from `sanity` and disables itself until a later successful develop validation enables it again. |
| [Develop - Nightly](workflows/develop-nightly.yml) | Dispatch from the `sanity` tag | Packages Linux and Windows runtime files from the captured validated commit using its matching build images, without rerunning their application tests. Builds the macOS package at the same SHA. Publishes the existing combined ZIP and separate macOS assets as the current `nightly` release. Then builds and deploys the directory image from that SHA to staging. |
| [Directory - Production promotion](workflows/directory-production.yml) | Push to `master` | Deploys the last successfully verified staging directory image by digest, without rebuilding it. Does not change game packaging. |
| [Release Artifact](workflows/master-release.yml) | Push to `master` or manual dispatch | Builds and packages a combined Linux and Windows runtime artifact using the release source's immutable tool versions. GitHub release asset publication is conditional on a tag-based invocation. |
| [Storage Cleanup](workflows/storage-cleanup.yml) | Weekly schedule or manual dispatch | Retains current GHCR build images and removes eligible old versions. Manual runs can also remove exact-name legacy Actions artifacts. |

## Pipeline concept

- Pull-request checks validate proposed changes with Linux/Docker only. Automatic Windows, macOS, and ARM64 verification runs after integration into `develop`, not as a pre-review or pre-merge gate.
- Develop validation establishes the `sanity` checkpoint. Nightly packaging uses that exact source revision and its build images, rather than whichever commit is newest when packaging runs.
- The scheduler separates successful validation from publication. The `nightly` tag and release represent the latest published nightly bundle, not a history of nightly releases. Replacement is non-transactional, so publication can temporarily leave the release unavailable.
- The `master` release-artifact path is separate from nightly publication. It produces a downloadable workflow artifact; a branch push does not itself publish a GitHub release.
- Directory deployment is separate from game hosting. Nightly staging and master promotion use one deployment queue and separate database/runtime identities. See [directory deployment operations](../docs/directory-cloud-run.md).
- Distribution builds select the directory through `D6R_DIRECTORY_DEFAULT_URL`. Nightly uses `https://staging.duel.netusite.cz` on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The existing Linux/Windows release workflow uses `https://duel.netusite.cz`, including manual release runs. There is no macOS caller in that release workflow. Channel selection is independent of build optimization. Other builds have no compiled default. Candidate directory checks use `run.app`; serving checks use the corresponding custom domain before staging eligibility or production success.

## Basic elements and workspace context

- **Containerized execution:** Linux builds and Windows cross-compilation use Docker build environments. Native Windows transport checks exercise the Windows implementation in a native Windows container.
- **Runners and images:** Self-hosted runners handle pull-request Linux validation, develop builds, and nightly work. GitHub-hosted runners support image publication, native Windows checks, scheduling, tagging, release-artifact builds, and storage cleanup. GHCR stores the reusable build images.
- **Artifacts and diagnostics:** Validation diagnostics, smoke evidence, and master transport artifacts are retained for seven days; nightly transport remains at one day. Global CTest logs are always preserved after a test failure. Per-test logs and screenshots are collected only for mapped failed tests, and graphical harnesses explicitly record their full-frame screenshot provenance. Only those recorded PNGs are retained, so comparison crops, normalized images, row/control extracts, and other generated derivatives are excluded regardless of filename.
- **Self-hosted Docker workspace contract:** The runner checkout and Docker daemon can occupy different filesystem namespaces, so the checkout path is not assumed to exist on the daemon host. The [workspace helper](../docker/run-with-daemon-workspace.sh) transfers source and build output through the Docker API. This relies on Docker daemon access and storage for the transferred workspace and output; a shared host path is not required.
- **Directory backend:** The Linux pull-request job builds the [verification container](../services/directory/README.md) from a Docker build context, without a checkout bind mount. Firebase CLI runs the application tests against the local Firestore emulator with a demo project and no cloud credentials. No deployment runs in this workflow.
- **Native dependencies:** Pull-request Linux validation builds its tool image from the checkout. Linux, MinGW and native MSVC use the same [pinned private Mbed TLS configuration](../docker/mbedtls/README.md) for both hosting kinds. The native Windows container builds its static dependency after mounted MSVC setup; the existing native CTests remain required by Develop - Sanity. Directory HTTPS uses separate libcurl builds and retains their crypto dependencies. Windows bundle packaging follows transitive DLL imports and retains the required dependency notices. Mbed TLS is static and its license is included in both bundles.
- **Native Windows channel checks:** The disposable container runs ordinary native CTests without gameplay certificate provisioning, trust-store changes or a certificate-test opt-in. No host trust store or user profile is mounted. Compiler and SDK mounts remain read-only. Automated transport checks do not prove graphical dedicated-session behavior.

## Tool image publication and selection

| GHCR package under `ghcr.io/mkapusnik-apps/duel6r/` | Tool recipe | Consumers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build` | `Dockerfile`, native amd64 | Linux sanity and Debug builds, ARM interoperability x86 helper, nightly, release |
| `build-arm64` | `Dockerfile`, native ARM64 | ARM candidate build and verification |
| `build-w64` | `Dockerfile.windows-cross` | Windows cross-compilation for nightly and release |
| `build-windows-transport` | `Dockerfile.windows-native-transport` | Windows transport verification with mounted host MSVC and SDK |

- Publication is separate from sanity. Each package publishes independently. A failure in one package does not cancel another. Only `develop`, while it is the default branch, can publish. Dispatches from other refs do not publish or move aliases.
- [Version selection](../docker/tool-image-version.sh) produces `tool-<64 lowercase hex characters>`. It hashes the committed Git tree records for the selected Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, `docker/mbedtls/`, and the version helper itself. Run it from the repository root. A shallow checkout is sufficient. Working-tree edits are not included until committed. Linux amd64 and ARM64 use the same input version in separate packages.
- Changes to these inputs trigger publication. Each job builds only if its version is absent. Writers to the same package are serialized to prevent version replacement. There are no application commits, build timestamps, or moving dependency branches in the version selector. The Windows cross recipe pins vcpkg to commit `9e593bb18ea69cc5095e012465dcd675a822ed0d` (release `2026.07.29`).
- A new version uses a fresh base pull and an uncached tool build. To refresh OS packages or a base image without another recipe change, increment the `Toolchain refresh revision` comment in the affected Dockerfile. Merge that change to `develop`. Manual dispatch does not rebuild an existing version. Do not overwrite or delete immutable tags to force a refresh.
- Build, packaging, smoke, and MinGW toolchain scripts run from the source checkout. Changes to those scripts do not require image publication. The Docker entrypoints require the checkout at `/workspace` or `C:\workspace`. Pull-request Linux checks continue to build an unpublished local tool image, so proposed tool changes and current checkout scripts are both checked.
- [Image resolution](../docker/resolve-tool-image.sh) reads the checked-out source's version, resolves the single-platform registry manifest to a digest, and supplies `image@sha256:...` to Docker. Sanity and ARM jobs wait up to two hours for a missing version. They fail at the deadline, or on other registry errors. They never substitute `latest` or rebuild a tool image. Sanity also requires the matching Windows cross image before advancing its tag.
- Nightly checks out the captured `sanity` commit before selecting tools. Release uses its own checked-out source. Both fail immediately if a required version is absent. Later publication cannot change their tool environment. Native Windows compiler and SDK versions remain supplied by the hosted runner and recorded by the existing helper; they are not frozen inside the tool image.
- `latest` is for interactive convenience only. CI consumers do not use it. Operate manual publication sequentially on current `develop`; do not rerun old publication jobs to move aliases backward. After a partial failure, inspect the package and workflow logs before rerunning. A rerun reuses versions already published and can complete the alias update.

### Initial bootstrap

1. Merge the lifecycle configuration to default `develop`. The new tool-input files trigger publication. Alternatively, dispatch `Develop - Build Container Image` from `develop` after the merge. No branch may bootstrap production aliases before integration.
2. Allow all four packages to publish. The workflow token needs package write access. New packages must allow this repository's workflows to read and administer them. Keep the existing native Windows Docker runner and read-only host-tool mounts.
3. Sanity can wait for publication. If publication exceeds the wait or fails, correct the failure, complete publication, and rerun sanity for the same source. Do not advance `sanity` manually or substitute an older image.
4. Use nightly only after a successful new sanity checkpoint. Older source refs continue to use their checked-in legacy workflows. Keep their protected legacy images during the transition. A release source with this lifecycle must have its tool inputs published from `develop` before release packaging.
5. Run storage cleanup in dry-run mode after all four packages exist and package Admin access is confirmed. Missing packages or denied inventory access stop cleanup. No automatic deletion of immutable tool versions is permitted.

## Develop sanity test groups

Each registered CTest has exactly one primary label from this table. Keep existing descriptive labels, timeouts, serial execution settings, and platform conditions.

| Group | Primary CTest label | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit / basic | `sanity-unit` | General helpers, resource checks, basic menu controls, and saved configuration/profile checks. The separate main-menu smoke also belongs to this job. It requires the full runtime, resources, Xvfb, and software rendering; it is not a pure unit test. |
| Common / local game | `sanity-common` | Existing offline Local Play checks: session setup, modes, roster/team behavior, rounds, rendering, animation, weapons, and world interactions where automated coverage exists. Includes both model checks and runtime journeys; this group does not certify complete solo-game end-to-end coverage. |
| Network / server-client | `sanity-network` | Host/client setup, transport, security, admission, authoritative state, replication, reconnect, directory interaction, and service/process lifecycle. Hosted-network solo continuation remains in this group, not Common. |

- The Linux jobs use the exact selectors `^sanity-unit$`, `^sanity-common$`, and `^sanity-network$`. Every registered test must be in one primary group, including tests without previous labels. Classify mixed suites by their behavior, not their filename or an existing `network`/`networking` label. Split registration where needed to separate basic settings checks from local-match journeys without dropping cases.
- Configuration checks use the existing `data/config.script` and `data/persons.json` formats. This grouping does not introduce INI support or change persistence rules.
- Each Linux job builds in its own disposable container from the source-selected tool digest. The jobs do not share a mutable build tree. The returned runtime bundle does not contain the CTest build tree, so independent jobs compile separately rather than transfer it. A failed group does not cancel the other matrix jobs.
- `docker/build.sh` accepts an optional `CTEST_LABEL_REGEX` when `RUN_TESTS=ON`. A selected group with no tests fails through CTest. With no selector, callers retain full-suite execution, including pull-request and ARM64 checks. CTest failure diagnostics retain their existing collection rules and have separate group artifact names.
- Platform is an execution overlay, not a fourth primary CTest label. Windows MSVC x64, Linux ARM64, and Apple Silicon and Intel x86_64 macOS retain their existing suites and platform-specific verification. They intentionally overlap the thematic groups. The Debug lint-equivalent build remains separate.
- All three Linux groups, the Debug build, and all platform jobs must pass before the `sanity` tag advances. These are post-integration gates. Pull-request wiring is unchanged. The existing macOS GUI/live cross-OS deferrals and ARM hardware acceptance limits still apply.

## Dedicated service boundary

- The [dedicated contract](../docs/network-play-first-release.md#public-dedicated-pilot) defines Linux x86-64 and Linux ARM64 packaged services. Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, Linux AArch64/Pi 5 and experimental Apple Silicon macOS 14+ and Intel x86_64 macOS 13 Ventura+ clients use the same encrypted channel for either hosting kind. Dedicated Windows/macOS hosting remains outside scope.
- The existing Linux runtime bundle supplies the server component. There is no separate dedicated Docker distribution or gameplay deployment workflow.
- An external operator supplies the direct gameplay listener and its connectable advertised endpoint under the [trust contract](../docs/network-trust-and-abuse-limits.md#encrypted-invite-only-public-pilot). Both hosting kinds use the common Mbed TLS EC-JPAKE channel and optional Password. No outer gameplay TLS frontend or PROXYv2 handoff is used. Source accounting uses the actual accepted TCP peer, not a peer-supplied source header. Plaintext traffic, legacy-profile retries and automatic unlocked retries remain prohibited.
- An unlocked connection encrypts traffic but does not authenticate the server against an active intermediary. A shared password does not distinguish one password holder from another. Directory HTTPS and its certificate verification are separate and remain required.
- The client uses an operator-supplied gameplay endpoint. Directory domains and compiled directory origins are not gameplay defaults. Repository preparation does not select a provider or domain, provision resources, or authorize billable activation.
- Native CLI and container results do not prove GUI or live cross-OS behavior. The Windows dedicated graphical journey remains required by the product acceptance contract; the macOS manual deferral below does not apply to Windows.

## ARM dedicated interoperability

- The ARM workflow builds both architectures from its source SHA. Its x86 companion job compiles only the existing client fixture and resolver. A tar artifact preserves their executable permissions and dynamic runtime dependencies. No x86 test campaign or shared image publication runs in that job.
- QEMU registers only `amd64`, with privileged preparation limited to the disposable GitHub-hosted ARM runner. The verification container is not privileged. It has no published ports, host trust store, user profile or Docker socket mount.
- Report the result as **native ARM service / QEMU-emulated x86 ELF client**. The production service and readiness probe stay native. The x86 client and its sibling resolver use emulation. Record the source SHA, workflow SHA and executable identities separately in the run logs.
- The existing public-dedicated process fixture runs its `--cross-architecture` selection. It owns direct loopback endpoints, protected passwords, resources and readiness sockets in one isolated container. It checks common-channel admission, controller state, Start, authoritative exchange, End, stale-session rejection and fresh reuse without a certificate relay or PROXY header. No external directory is needed. This is not a cloud deployment or physical Pi acceptance.
- Native ARM CTests must also exercise native ARM-client participation. The emulated x86 companion does not establish native ARM-client behavior or physical Pi GPU, input or audio acceptance.
- Automatic verification still runs after integration and gates `sanity`. Manual candidate verification does not add a branch-protection requirement. The operator must dispatch the authorized checkpoint and compare its run head before accepting evidence.

## Experimental macOS build and nightly

- The [macOS contract](../docs/macos.md) defines Apple Silicon macOS 14+ and Intel x86_64 macOS 13 Ventura+, Release, `gl1`, local play, and the approved Host, direct Join, and Browse IPv4 networking scope. The native execution exception includes automated network verification on each architecture. Linux and Windows keep their existing Docker paths.
- The reusable build uses separate native jobs: ARM64 on `macos-14` and Intel x86_64 on `macos-15-intel`. A failed job does not cancel the other architecture. The ARM64 image retires on **2026-11-02**. Its replacement remains a separate follow-up. The application and all bundled dependencies must preserve the target minimum: macOS 14.0 for ARM64 and macOS 13.0 Ventura for Intel. A newer build host does not change that minimum. Changing only the application deployment target is not sufficient.
- Homebrew installs only the build tools: CMake, Ninja, and pkg-config. CI provisions Python 3.13 with `actions/setup-python@v7` using the host architecture. It passes the action's absolute `python-path` output as `D6R_PYTHON` to preparation and build helpers, prints the version, executable, and machine architecture, and checks the 3.13 version. Helpers use that executable for Python commands and pass it as `Python3_EXECUTABLE` to CMake. CTest lists the registered certificate-fixture and native-trust commands before test execution so the selected interpreter is visible. Direct native builds use the documented Homebrew `python@3.13` executable by default; to select another installed interpreter, export its absolute path as `D6R_PYTHON` before both helper commands. Do not rely on PATH alone to select CMake's interpreter.
- The native runner supplies Xcode and system tools, including make, Perl, patch, and curl. CI runs `D6R_MACOS_ARCH=<architecture> bash macos/prepare-runtime-dependencies.sh`. This [dependency helper](../macos/prepare-runtime-dependencies.sh) first runs the portable `MacPackagingTests.py` checks once, before expensive dependency compilation. It then builds a private runtime prefix from the [pinned source closure](../macos/runtime-sources.json), including multimedia libraries and OpenSSL. It verifies source checksums and notices and uses the target architecture and deployment floor. It does not use Homebrew runtime bottles. OpenSSL installation includes `install_sw` and `install_ssldirs`. The helper checks that the private `ssl/openssl.cnf` exists and is not empty, then runs the shared certificate preflight with the private OpenSSL executable. The preflight uses its own configuration and checks certificate/key readability and PEM/DER equivalence; it does not prove installation completeness or native SecTrust behavior. Each native job has a 90-minute limit for dependency compilation, application verification, and packaging.
- The [native build helper](../macos/build.sh) owns application tests, package checks, and dependency bundling. CI sets `D6R_MACOS_ARCH` to `arm64` or `x86_64` and invokes `D6R_SOURCE_REVISION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" bash macos/build.sh` after dependency preparation. Package checks must enforce the architecture and its minimum macOS version for every bundled binary. Source-build configuration alone is not runtime compatibility evidence.
- The helper builds static Mbed TLS 3.6.7 from the [common pinned recipe](../docker/mbedtls/CMakeLists.txt) with the private hardware-only AES profile. Directory HTTPS uses a separate private shared libcurl 8.21.0 from [the source-pinned recipe](../macos/build-curl.sh), not the Homebrew libcurl keg. The recipe verifies archive SHA-256 `ad6f2f94934b38e31e48272833c99b891d045b4565fe942a53fbd27bd3910e16`, uses the private source-built OpenSSL, and enables Apple SecTrust and threaded asynchronous DNS without a CA bundle, CA path, or OpenSSL CA fallback. Both private dependency builds use the selected native SDK, target architecture, and its deployment target (14.0 for ARM64; 13.0 for Intel). The helper selects the private curl headers and dylib explicitly and records its configuration and identity in dependency build metadata.
- Keep certificate-chain and hostname verification enabled. Native trust checks must observe actual SecTrust evaluation; an HTTPS success with zero observed native evaluations is not proof of Apple system trust. The package must include the non-system dependency closure and licenses without a dependency on build-machine Homebrew paths.
- The reusable workflow passes `directory_default_url` to the helper as `D6R_DIRECTORY_DEFAULT_URL`. The helper must pass it to the same CMake option. The default is empty for develop validation and other unchannelled builds; the nightly caller supplies staging. A release-channel invocation must supply `https://duel.netusite.cz`; it must not infer the channel from `Release` optimization.
- Each job produces `build/macos/Duel 6 Reloaded.app` and `build/macos/duel6r-macos-<architecture>.zip` with its `.sha256` file. ARM64 keeps `build-info.json`; Intel supplies `build-info-x86_64.json` in the same output directory. CI transfers the archive and metadata, not the unarchived application. Develop validation artifacts last seven days. Nightly transport artifacts last one day.
- Failed jobs upload `macos-failure-diagnostics-<architecture>` for seven days. It contains the last 1 MiB of each available preparation, build, interpreter-listing, CTest, and package log, plus the complete CTest `LastTest.log` and `LastTestsFailed.log` when present. Phase headings identify the active operation. CTest failure output is limited to 32 KiB per test, with middle truncation; test failures still stop packaging. Do not upload dependency trees, test homes, certificates, private keys, or environment dumps. Full command output remains in the job log.
- Develop validation builds the integrated push SHA. Nightly builds use the captured `sanity` SHA for every platform. Publication waits for the existing Linux/Windows package and both macOS packages. The release retains `duel6r-nightly.zip`, `duel6r-macos-arm64.zip`, `duel6r-macos-arm64.zip.sha256`, and `build-info.json`. It adds `duel6r-macos-x86_64.zip`, `duel6r-macos-x86_64.zip.sha256`, and `build-info-x86_64.json`.
- No Apple signing identity, notarization credentials, or new repository secrets are required. The macOS artifact is experimental unsigned distribution, not verified platform support. Use the artifact's launch instructions and macOS approval procedure; do not disable system-wide security protections.
- Native automated transport, security, process, build, and package verification runs on both architectures after integration in Develop - Sanity at the push SHA. It must pass before `sanity` advances and the nightly scheduler is enabled; it is not a pre-review or pre-merge gate. Use the existing Mac job and application-owned CTest registration. Skipped, Linux-only, or other-architecture results do not establish native behavior for an architecture. No separate readiness workflow is required.
- The user performs actual Mac GUI and live cross-OS verification on both architectures after merge and the subsequent nightly publication, including manual launch, gameplay, saved-data, and visual checks. These checks are deferred, not passed. Native CLI results do not prove Finder launch, input, audio, rendering, graphical host/join, or live cross-OS gameplay. Actual release-asset evidence follows publication.

## Storage cleanup safeguards

- Scheduled runs apply GHCR cleanup; manual runs default to a dry run. The workflow fully inventories all four tool packages and resolves `develop`, `sanity`, and `nightly` before deleting anything. It keeps the newest 10 versions, `latest`, legacy `develop` and protected exact-SHA tags, and **every** `tool-<64 lowercase hex characters>` tag.
- Immutable tool versions do not expire. This protects develop, sanity, nightly, and all release sources without a second version-derivation algorithm in cleanup. Storage grows only when tool inputs change. Any future pruning policy needs a separate change that preserves source reproducibility; do not manually delete these versions.
- GHCR cleanup needs `contents: read`, `packages: write`, and repository package Admin access to all four packages listed above. Ref, inventory, metadata, authentication, or authorization failures stop cleanup.
- Legacy Actions artifact cleanup is manual-only, defaults to `skip`, requires `actions: write`, fully paginates the inventory, and deletes only the exact legacy names listed in the workflow. It does not delete current transport artifacts, diagnostics, smoke evidence, Docker build records, or release assets.

This overview describes the pipeline's responsibilities and relationships, not procedures for implementing individual steps.
